source_review.notes: Reviewed current PostgreSQL 18 explicit-locking and pg_locks documentation; MySQL 8.4 InnoDB lock/locking-read documentation; current SQL Server 17 locking/versioning guidance; the original Gray et al. multiple-granularity paper; Graefe's B-tree locking survey; IBM's ARIES/IM record; the Cahill SSI paper; and the Bernstein-Hadzilacos-Goodman text archive. All ten cited destinations were retrieved successfully and retained locally after correcting Graefe's DOI to 10.1145/1806907.1806908. Product behavior is explicitly version/current-documentation scoped.

evidence: Checked resource hierarchy, parent, canonical modes, compatibility, held/waiting requests, conversion join, escalation, footprint, convoy, and starvation definitions.
Checked the complete canonical IS/IX/S/SIX/X matrix for mode meanings and symmetry.
Checked logical lock, physical latch, MVCC version, predicate dependency, key range, and advisory lock distinctions.
Checked product-specific PostgreSQL, InnoDB, and SQL Server mode names are never treated as aliases of the teaching lattice.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Compatibility is explicitly only one part of a protocol; duration, hierarchy, fairness, conversion, and deadlock policy remain separate.

evidence: Independently reconstructed all five compatibility rows from a separate symmetric representation.
Independently verified IS permits (IS,IX,S,SIX), IX permits (IS,IX), S permits (IS,S), SIX permits IS, and X permits none.
Independently evaluated T3 table S against T1 IS plus T2 IX as blocked.
Independently evaluated T4 row-A X against T1 row-A S as blocked and printed independent_invariants=True.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The independent calculation did not import or execute the chapter implementation.

evidence: Re-derived each compatibility row from whether the broad node claim can coexist with announced descendant reads/writes.
Re-derived hierarchy safety: every descendant writer's ancestor IX conflicts with an ancestor S/X request.
Re-derived fine concurrency: ancestor IX/IX coexist while distinct leaf X resources do not conflict.
Re-derived escalation safety as acquire sufficient covering ancestor mode before releasing descendants.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The hierarchy proof assumes canonical shared resource identities and universal ancestor-protocol compliance.

evidence: Reviewed same/different owner, same/different row, missing ancestors, invalid early ancestor release, S-to-X conversion, two upgraders, queue fairness, timeout, NOWAIT, SKIP LOCKED, and cancellation.
Reviewed empty/range predicates, endpoints, duplicates, NULL/collation/operator class, access-path changes, record/gap/next-key/insert-intention, spatial predicates, and partition crossing.
Reviewed tiny/huge scans, skew/hot keys, row/page/table/partition choice, lock memory, failed/successful escalation, mixed S/X descendants, disabling escalation, and safe batching.
Reviewed advisory-key collision/encoding, session/transaction scope, pool reuse, DDL/schema modes, connection loss, deadlock victim, recovery, observation races, blocker chains, and latches.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Every recommendation preserves the invariant and atomic boundary before considering lock count or blocking reduction.

evidence: The repository verifier matched exact ten-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
The model checks canonical matrix output, compatible table intentions, blocked coarse reader, blocked same-row writer, and exact wait queue.
Manual review checked canonical resource identity, ancestor intention, all-holder compatibility, conversion/escalation no-gap, predicate coverage, duration, and wait outcome requirements.
Draft validation accepted exact front matter, section order, ten examples, five exercises/answers, local links, citations, and executable evidence before stopping only for review evidence.
invariant_checking.notes: The model trusts hierarchy callers and omits same-owner conversion, duration, fairness, deadlock, concurrency, predicate ranges, product modes, recovery, and performance.

evidence: Reviewed intention-advertisement safety and every compatibility premise line by line.
Reviewed disjoint leaf concurrency and same-leaf exclusion reasoning.
Reviewed escalation overlap/coverage and mixed-mode strength requirements.
Reviewed all exercise answers for matrix derivation, hierarchy repair, escalation diagnosis, invariant protection, and cross-engine evidence.
proof_review.notes: No proof of vendor lock-manager correctness, fairness, deadlock freedom, lock-plan completeness, predicate coverage implementation, or production performance is claimed.

evidence: The executable matrix is explicitly a canonical teaching model rather than a product implementation.
The hierarchy and escalation arguments state compliance, identity, containment, and coverage assumptions.
Predicate lock is separated into blocking range protection versus nonblocking SSI dependency tracking.
Audited locks, protects, exclusive, compatible, safe, exact, guarantees, current, complete, and optimal language for scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Operational examples do not infer durable lock behavior from hints or isolated instantaneous monitoring snapshots.

evidence: The standard-library compatibility/wait model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
A separate compatibility representation independently reproduced matrix rows and both waits.
All ten cited destinations were successfully retrieved and retained locally.
Production conclusions require engine/version, transaction/query/plan, resource/mode, wait graph, duration, lock count/memory, escalation, abort/retry, latch, invariant, and latency evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live lock manager, transaction, conversion, range lock, escalation, advisory lock, cancellation, deadlock, recovery, DMV/pg_locks snapshot, or benchmark was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives multiple-granularity safety from intention modes while separating modes, hierarchy, resource identity, duration, conversion, escalation, predicates, and physical latches.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed current PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQL Server semantics, granularity tradeoffs, escalation, conversions, ranges, wait policies, advisory locks, pooling, observability, deterministic tests, and capacity risks.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, executable matrix/trace, ten distinct examples, and five exercises progress from compatibility through hierarchy proofs, escalation diagnosis, invariant-specific designs, and cross-engine verification.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter does not certify a vendor lock lattice, lock manager, plan/resource mapping, predicate/range coverage, escalation/conversion policy, advisory protocol, wait/deadlock behavior, observability result, benchmark, or production configuration.
